notes: PLACEHOLDER TUNING (mw-e09.2) — starting numbers for the visibility model, to tune in play (mw-e09.6 authors the full stealth table). Light: the target's samples blend halfway between their mean and their brightest (a lit head shows), then dark vision lifts what the observer sees; the curve keeps deep shadow nearly invisible (level 0.15 reads 0.05) and is close to linear from half light to full (0.5 → 0.45, 1 → 1). A humanoid (dark vision 0.2) sees 0.05 light as 0.24. Stance: standing 1, crouched 0.5, prone 0.25. Motion bands match the controller's gaits (mw-e02.10) so stance × motion reproduces its visibility table: still 0.8 below 0.2 m/s, slow walk 0.85 from 0.2, walk 0.9 from 1.6 (above the 1.2 slow walk and 1.5 light-stick speeds), run 1.0 from 2.5 and sprint 1.0 from 6.0. Profile: a cloak hides to 0.7, a disguise to 0.8 (on top of the equipment brightness the wearer supplies). Distance: no falloff to 8 m, 0.75 at 20 m (the humanoid far range), 0.4 at 40 m and 0.1 at 80 m and beyond. Contrast: a target at or below 0.2 light against background light of 0.7 or more gains 0.3 on its light term (never above the full-light term). Noise (mw-e09.3, PLACEHOLDER): a sound loses 20·log10(d) dB over a path of d metres (none within 1 m), then the gain of every door, wall and floor it passes. Doors: open 0, ajar −6, closed −20 (the bead's numbers); an iron leaf muffles a little more (ajar −8, closed −25) and a stone slab more still (ajar −8, closed −28). Walls −30 by default (stone −35, wood −18); floors and ceilings −25 by default (wood −15: a footstep upstairs carries through planks; stone −35). Below 10 dB a sound is not heard and propagation stops searching. Impacts (mw-e03.25): below 1 J nothing is heard (a settling pile); a 10 J impact on stone is 60 dB (a dropped sword; a shield thrown down about 64), and every ten times the energy adds 10 dB (a 200 J crate 73 dB, a 7.8 kJ chandelier 89 dB); the louder of the two materials' surface offsets (their footstepLoudness: glass +12, iron +6, wood +2, cloth -8) is added; nothing exceeds 100 dB. Footsteps (mw-e09.5): one step is the gait's level at 1 m on stone (sneak 25, walk 40, run 55, sprint 65) plus the surface offset (carpet -10, gravel +8) plus the equipment term, 20·log10 of the wearer's noise multiplier (ADR-0003: Medium +2.3 dB, Heavy +4.1 dB, applied once, clamped to 0.5-2.0 so at most +6 dB); a creature has no controller, so its gait is read from its speed (0.2 m/s a walk, 2.5 a run, 6 a sprint). A landing is a step-sized thud from half a metre up (30 dB), 45 dB from a metre (an ordinary jump), 60 dB from 2 m, 70 dB from 3 m and 95 dB from 10 m, plus the surface and equipment terms. Hollow boards creak on a seeded roll (surface table); the per-step varianceDb of the table is not rolled, so a step's loudness is exactly what the formula says.
